sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Wiarumus language' (accessed 2026-09-17).
sources.note: No phonology; notes only villagers born before ca. 1940 speak it; cites Ethnologue 25, PARADISEC DL2 and WF3.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG [Summer Institute of Linguistics, Papua New Guinea Branch]. 2007. Endangered languages listing: Wiarumus [tua]. Ukarumpa: SIL (web document, 3 pp., 'Last updated: 15 Feb 2007 (IDT)').
sources.note: No phonology content. Sociolinguistic vitality note (Tok Pisin shift; only a minority of the older generation understood Wiarumus in 2002), report of a June 2002 SIL alphabet design workshop in Mandi, and a resource list: 'Spelling guide (Arminen and Hoel 2002b); book of Wiarumus stories, with Wiarumus - Tok Pisin dictionary (507 entries) appended (Arminen et al 2002)'. Its value is as the pointer to works 2-4.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. 2007-2013 [Internet Archive copy 2016-03-02]. PNG Language Resources: Wiarumus [tua] (language resources page); with Ethnologue 15th ed. (Gordon 2005) web entry 'Wiarumus' [Internet Archive copy 2009-01-30].
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: SIL-PNG page: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' -> confirms no Organised Phonology Data, data paper, dictionary or survey report was ever released by SIL for Wiarumus. Ethnologue 15: population 162 (1981), 'Only people over 60 are still speakers.. Interest in revitalization', 'Roman script'; no phonology.

sources.citation: Sanders, Arden G. & Joy Sanders. 1980. Defining the centres of the Marienberg language family. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 20, Pacific Linguistics A-56: 171-196.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistics (Mandi 41% with Muniwara, 25% average cognates) and sociolinguistic/schooling notes (sec. 5.2.6 Mandi); no phonology.

sources.citation: Sanders, Joy & Arden G. Sanders. 1980. Dialect survey of the Kamasau language. Pacific Linguistics A-56: 137-170.
sources.note: Nothing relevant: covers Kamasau villages only; Mandi/Wiarumus not mentioned; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 767-780. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. p.769 phylum-level phonological characterisation (three places of articulation, usually no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, high proportion of fricatives) makes no mention of stress; Mandi is named only as a Marienberg language apparently lacking gender (p.772) and in the family list.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik Languages: Checklist and Preliminary Classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (hdl 1885/146478)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 55 MANDI (printed p.17, p.21): village Mandi, pop. 162, 'Comments: Test DCL71 (Anton Manuwonk, Martin/Mandi)'; classification checklist only.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific Fascicle Five. Anthropological Linguistics 7(9). Bloomington: Indiana University (ERIC document ED010365, 124 pp.). Section 'Unclassified languages of the Sepik District' (names and comments 'from Capell (1962)'), entry 'Mandi', p.58.
sources.note: Nothing. The Mandi entry is a location/population/multilingualism note (80 speakers, all also speaking Boikin, Terebu and Tumara); the section preface says 'Little or no linguistic work has been done on most of the non-Austronesian languages of the Sepik District'. The whole file was a full-text search for stress/accent/tonal: the only hits are in the general introduction and in other families' sections, none tied to Mandi or the Marienberg group.
